text:
Alex (infra): Quick heads-up: nightly billing+util report shows reserved GPU commitments misaligned with hosted API demand in EU. We should triage before renewals.

Maria (capacity): numbers?

Alex (infra): Committed: 140 A100-equiv total (eu-west + us-west). Last 7d util: overall 58%. us-west 62 reserved, used 28 (45% util). eu-west 78 reserved, used 73 (94% util) -> p99 queue ~2.3s. Hosted prod traffic growing ~22% MoM in EU.

Kevin (sre): ouch. Are those unused GPUs actually billed as committed hours? any tag mismatches?

Finance-bot: running commit-attachment audit... found ~6.1% of committed hours unlinked due to missing project tags and transient test instances.

Jin (billing): that equates to ~$18.6k/month in lost discounts. Also found ephemeral test clusters launching reserved-class GPUs without policies.

Paul (eng-runtime): we can add an admission webhook to block reserved-class SKU launches from non-prod namespaces + an infra policy to require tags. Low-risk.

Sana (product): For customers in EU who depend on low latency, can we avoid cross-region routing? Any fallback will need comms.

Alex (infra): short-term options I'm proposing:
- fix tag attachment mapping (recoup commit discounts)
- block reserved SKU usage in dev/test via webhook + quota rules
- enable soft fallback routing for best-effort traffic to us-west (configurable percent)
- request 30d marketplace burst or convertible short-term commit if gap persists
- re-evaluate before next renewal window with updated forecast

Maria (capacity): forecast: if current growth continues, EU needs +30 A100-equiv in 90d to hit p99<2s. If we recover ~6 from billing fixes and shift 12 from us-west, remaining gap ~12.

Jin (billing): gap remedies: buy modest reserved ramp in EU at next 30d renewal (12-16), request temporary burst, or negotiate a convertible commit (60-90d).

Kevin (sre): runtime mitigation: throttle batch concurrency and reduce background aggregator jobs to free host capacity for low-latency paths. Could buy 1-2 weeks of runway.

Paul (eng-runtime): will stage webhook to dev and then alpha in staging.

Alex (infra): proposed test: route 20% of best-effort EU traffic to us-west fallback for 72h, enable webhook, and monitor. Runbook snippet: 
```
- infra/routers/fallback.enabled=true
- infra/routers/fallback.pct=20
- admission: deny reserved-sku in namespaces where label env in [dev, test]
- monitor: dashboard/infra/capacity-eu, alerts on p99>2s or errors+5%
```

Sana (product): I'll draft a customer advisory template for strict-region SLAs in case we need to escalate.

Maria (capacity): I'll update the renewal model (spreadsheet) with the recovered discount assumption and the 30-day burst option.

Finance-bot: estimated recoverable commit credits: $18,600/mo if tag fixes applied (pending cloud provider confirmation).

Kevin (sre): starting the 72h soft fallback now. Will post p99 and error-rate snapshots every 6h.

Ops-bot: automated runbook step: created monitoring playbook at infra-playbooks/commit-recon.

Alex (infra): decision criteria: if gap >10% after 30d, recommend converting 12-16 on-demand -> reserved in EU at next commit. If <10%, close after 60d.

Jin (billing): noted. I'll also add a cloud policy request to block untagged reserved attachments.

Kevin (sre): monitoring and rolling notes incoming. Thanks team.

Sana (product): thanks all — ping me if customers need a proactive notice.
